details.aspect: Narcobloqueos close the world at an hour's notice
details.description: Vehicles burned across highways shut cities and regions, stranding work, school and medical travel with no warning and no appeal.
details.energy_note: The roads close and nobody announces when they reopen.

details.aspect: Buses stopped, young men taken off
details.description: Passenger transport interception - people removed from buses at checkpoints that are not state checkpoints - is a documented route into DES-001, notably in Tamaulipas.
details.energy_note: The bus stops and two seats are empty afterwards.

details.aspect: SCENE - the road closed at four
details.description: Burning trucks across the highway at both ends of the valley. No announcement, no timetable, no authority to ask. His wife is on the other side of it with the baby, at the clinic. He waits at the edge of the blockade with forty other people until nine at night.
details.energy_note: Five hours at a roadblock nobody official declared.

issues.title: La Bestia, and being cargo
issues.category_name: Transit through Mexico: the train, the kidnap, the ransom
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by being male
issues.summary: Transit migrants riding freight trains through Mexico - mostly young men - exposed to mutilation, kidnapping and extortion along the whole length of the country.

details.aspect: The train is the cheapest and it removes limbs
details.description: Riding on top of freight trains is free and produces falls, amputations and deaths. Shelters along the route treat the survivors.
details.energy_note: Free passage, at the price of a leg.

details.aspect: Kidnapping for ransom against relatives abroad
details.description: Migrants are taken and held while relatives in the US are called for payment - a business model that requires the victim to have someone who loves him and a phone number.
details.energy_note: Held until his brother in Houston pays.

details.aspect: Reporting is impossible by design
details.description: The victim is himself irregular in Mexico, so the complaint goes to authorities who may deport him - and, per DES/POL, may be involved.
details.energy_note: The police are the second problem, not the solution.

details.aspect: SCENE - the shelter in Coatzacoalcos
details.description: A Honduran boy, maybe seventeen, with his forearm bandaged from where the train took the skin off. He is worried about the bandage because it makes him identifiable, and being identifiable is the thing he is most afraid of - more than the arm.
details.energy_note: Frightened of the bandage more than the injury.

issues.title: San Fernando: two hundred and sixty-five people
issues.category_name: Transit through Mexico: the train, the kidnap, the ransom
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by being male
issues.summary: The 2010 and 2011 massacres in Tamaulipas, the police involvement, and the fact that they remain effectively unpunished.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - 2010: seventy-two
details.description: In August 2010, 72 undocumented migrants - 58 men and 14 women, from Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Ecuador and Brazil - were murdered by Los Zetas at a ranch in San Fernando, shot in the back of the head and piled together. It was discovered because one wounded survivor reached a checkpoint on 23 August. The police chief leading the investigation was later killed.
details.energy_note: Discovered only because one man survived and walked.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - 2011: one hundred and ninety-three
details.description: In March 2011, 193 people were killed at La Joya ranch, taken in hijackings of passenger buses on Federal Highway 101 and buried in 47 clandestine mass graves. The investigation began because luggage went unclaimed in Reynosa and Matamoros. By 7 June 2011, 193 bodies had been recovered.
details.energy_note: It came to light because suitcases were not collected.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the police helped
details.description: Federal prosecutors indicated local police in San Fernando were involved in the 2011 massacres, per a memo from the Attorney General's Office obtained under transparency laws. Detained Zetas reportedly said local police assisted in 'intercepting of people'.
details.energy_note: The police stopped the buses.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - and nothing was published about punishment
details.description: Amnesty International noted five years on that authorities had made arrests but failed to publish any information as to whether anyone had been sentenced, describing Mexico as becoming a 'no-go zone' for migrants. A year after the 2011 graves, 49 torsos, several believed to be migrants, were found in Cadereyta, Nuevo León.
details.energy_note: Arrests, and no published sentence.

issues.title: The migrants who are not Mexican, in Mexico
issues.category_name: Transit through Mexico: the train, the kidnap, the ransom
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Mexico, any gender
issues.summary: Mexico as a transit and now destination country, including flows the brief asked about from outside the Americas.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the Chinese route through Mexico
details.description: Border Patrol encountered 330 mainland Chinese migrants between ports of entry in FY2021; in 2023 it was 24,050. Many flew to Ecuador, which required no visa, then to Tijuana, paying around $400 for a drive to a gap in the fence; others paid $7,000-10,000 for routes through the Darién Gap. Crossings fell to 1,326 by September 2024.
details.energy_note: From Guangdong to Tijuana, via Quito.

details.aspect: THE HONEST GAP - Chinese state media largely did not cover it
details.description: The brief asked for Chinese agency sources. Searching for Xinhua, CGTN or Global Times coverage of Chinese migrants at the US-Mexico border surfaced none; the reporting is Western and Hong Kong outlets. The absence is recorded rather than papered over with a substitute.
details.energy_note: The Chinese agencies did not report it.

details.aspect: Mexico as the enforcer of someone else's border
details.description: Mexican enforcement against third-country nationals is shaped by US policy and trade leverage, so Mexico polices a border that is not its own, against people who did not intend to stay.
details.energy_note: Policing a frontier belonging to another country.

issues.title: Beaten into saying it
issues.category_name: Police, military, torture and arbitrary detention
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
issues.summary: Torture and ill-treatment in Mexican custody is not anecdotal - it has been measured by the national statistics institute, in a survey of the prison population, and the numbers are extraordinary.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - ENPOL 2021
details.description: 42% of incarcerated people reported being beaten or ill-treated at the public prosecutor's office to incriminate themselves or admit false claims; 22% said they were coerced into incriminating others; 20% stated they pleaded guilty as a result.
details.energy_note: Four in ten, beaten into confessing.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the wider 2016 figure
details.description: The World Justice Project, working with INEGI, found that from 2006 to 2016, 79% of people deprived of liberty were tortured or mistreated during detention, transfer or their stay in the Public Ministry. The sample covered 51,658 inmates, representative of 187,784 people.
details.energy_note: Seventy-nine per cent, over a decade.

details.aspect: The two numbers measure different things
details.description: The 79% figure covers broad ill-treatment across all stages; the 42% is specifically coercive beating aimed at self-incrimination at the prosecutor's office. ENPOL asked about being punched or kicked, beaten with an object, burned, electrically shocked, crushed, cut or shot, or forced into sexual activity; some researchers exclude punching and kicking to separate excessive force from torture proper.
details.energy_note: Both numbers are real and they count different things.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - due process failure predicts torture, quantifiably
details.description: When a detained person is not allowed to contact a family member, the frequency of torture increases by 16%; if the person does not contact a lawyer, by 21%. The procedural safeguard and the beating are directly linked.
details.energy_note: No phone call, and the odds of being beaten rise measurably.

details.aspect: The victim has to prove it happened
details.description: The UN Committee against Torture noted that confessions extracted under torture were substantial, with victims themselves obliged to prove torture occurred - after being held incommunicado by the people they must prove it against.
details.energy_note: He must prove it, against the people who held him.

details.aspect: He will be examined by a doctor who works for them
details.description: Medical documentation of torture depends on examination by institutionally independent clinicians; where the examiner is employed by the same authority, the record that would prove it is produced by the accused party.
details.energy_note: Examined for injuries by their own doctor.

issues.title: The soldier doing police work
issues.category_name: Police, military, torture and arbitrary detention
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Mexico, any gender
issues.summary: Two decades of military deployment for domestic public security, with troops trained for war carrying out stops, searches and arrests.

details.aspect: Soldiers are not trained to arrest people
details.description: Military doctrine is built around defeating an enemy, not gathering evidence and preserving a chain of custody, and the outcomes differ accordingly.
details.energy_note: Trained to win, deployed to arrest.

details.aspect: Military justice investigating military conduct
details.description: Where soldiers are investigated at all, the process has historically run through military channels, which is the structure described in assets/text/abuse as POL-005.
details.energy_note: Investigated by their own.
details.notes: Cross-reference assets/text/abuse POL-005.

details.aspect: The checkpoint is the routine encounter
details.description: Young men are stopped, searched and questioned at military and National Guard checkpoints as an ordinary condition of travel in much of the country.
details.energy_note: Searched on the way to work, by an army.

details.aspect: SCENE - hands on the truck
details.description: Eighteen-year-old soldier, rifle across his chest, asking him to step out. He puts his hands on the hot metal without being told, because he has done this before and knows it shortens it. The soldier is younger than his son.
details.energy_note: Knows the posture that makes it end faster.

issues.title: Reporting a crime, and what it costs to bother
issues.category_name: Police, military, torture and arbitrary detention
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Mexico, any gender
issues.summary: The cifra negra: the overwhelming majority of crime in Mexico is never reported, and the reason is a rational assessment of what reporting achieves.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the extortion dark figure
details.description: INEGI estimates 97% of extortion offences went unreported in 2023, and ENVIPE 2025 similarly estimates 97% never reported, due to fear and distrust of authorities. For crimes against businesses the dark figure reached 96.7% in ENVIPE 2024.
details.energy_note: Ninety-seven per cent of it never reaches anyone.

details.aspect: The complaint costs a day and produces a folder
details.description: Filing a denuncia requires hours at a ministerio público, produces a file number, and in most cases nothing further.
details.energy_note: A day gone, and a reference number.

details.aspect: Reporting can be the dangerous act
details.description: Where police are involved with the people complained about - see MIG-002 - reporting identifies the complainant to them.
details.energy_note: The report reaches the wrong desk on purpose.

issues.title: Arraigo and being held before being charged
issues.category_name: Police, military, torture and arbitrary detention
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
issues.summary: Pre-charge detention for investigation, long criticised internationally, which inverts the normal sequence of accusation and evidence.

details.aspect: Detention in order to build the case
details.description: Arraigo permitted holding a person while evidence was gathered, rather than gathering evidence in order to hold them.
details.energy_note: Held first, investigated afterwards.

details.aspect: It was the subject of sustained international criticism
details.description: UN bodies and the Inter-American system repeatedly criticised the figure as incompatible with presumption of innocence, and its scope has been narrowed by successive rulings.
details.energy_note: Condemned repeatedly, for years.

details.aspect: Weeks of detention leave no conviction and no record to clear
details.description: A man released without charge has lost the job and the weeks, and has no finding to appeal because there was never a finding.
details.energy_note: Nothing to appeal, because nothing was ever decided.

details.aspect: SCENE - forty days
details.description: He is released with no charge after five and a half weeks. Nobody apologises, nobody explains, and there is no document recording that he was innocent - because nobody ever formally said he was not. The job is gone and the landlord has let the room.
details.energy_note: Released without a piece of paper saying he did nothing.

issues.title: Imprisoned without a sentence
issues.category_name: The justice system: pretrial detention, arraigo, the prison
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
issues.summary: Automatic pretrial detention - prisión preventiva oficiosa - jails people on the category of the accusation rather than on any individual assessment. Roughly half of Mexico's unsentenced prisoners are held this way.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the current numbers
details.description: At the close of 2025, 42.2% of people deprived of liberty in Mexico were without a sentence: of 231,436 people in prison, 97,722 had no judicial resolution, and of those, 50.1% were under prisión preventiva oficiosa (INEGI Censo Nacional del Sistema Penitenciario 2026).
details.energy_note: Ninety-seven thousand people, not convicted of anything.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the sex split, which runs against the usual direction
details.description: Among the unsentenced, 34.5% of men and 31.5% of women were in justified preventive detention, while 49.7% of men and 55.2% of women were under PPO. Automatic detention falls proportionally harder on women; the absolute numbers are overwhelmingly men.
details.energy_note: Proportionally worse for women, numerically almost all men.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - two states apply it to everyone
details.description: Estado de México and Michoacán reported that 100% of their unsentenced prison population was under prisión preventiva oficiosa - 12,349 people and 3,044 people respectively.
details.energy_note: One hundred per cent, in two states.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the catalogue keeps growing
details.description: PPO entered the Constitution in 2008; a later reform to Article 19 expanded the list of qualifying offences to include extortion, false tax receipts, fuel theft and fentanyl-related crimes. The prison population rose from 235,197 at end-2024 to 256,127 at end-2025.
details.energy_note: Every expansion of the list fills more cells.

details.aspect: It is punishment that precedes the finding
details.description: A man accused of a listed offence is imprisoned from the start of proceedings without a judge analysing his individual case, even absent solid evidence or any procedural risk. If acquitted years later, the years are simply gone.
details.energy_note: Acquitted in 2029, having been in prison since 2025.

details.aspect: Waiting in prison changes the plea
details.description: Where the wait for trial exceeds the likely sentence, pleading guilty is the faster route out - so PPO manufactures convictions independently of guilt, which is the mechanism behind POL-001's 20% who pleaded guilty.
details.energy_note: Confessing because it is quicker than being innocent.

issues.title: The overcrowded cell
issues.category_name: The justice system: pretrial detention, arraigo, the prison
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
issues.summary: Mexican prisons at record population with overcrowding concentrated in a subset of facilities, holding a population that is over 90% male.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the record and the concentration
details.description: The prison population reached nearly 260,000, a historic record, with overcrowding concentrated in 140 of 275 penitentiary centres.
details.energy_note: Half the prisons hold more than they can.

details.aspect: Self-governance inside
details.description: Where staffing is inadequate, internal order is delegated in practice to whoever can enforce it, so the cell block is governed by the same structures as CAR-002.
details.energy_note: The wing is taxed like the road outside.

details.aspect: The family pays for him to be inside
details.description: Food, phone credit, protection and basic goods are bought by relatives, so imprisonment is an ongoing expense to a household that has also lost his income.
details.energy_note: They pay weekly for him to survive being held.

issues.title: A record that closes the rest of his life
issues.category_name: The justice system: pretrial detention, arraigo, the prison
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
issues.summary: Carta de no antecedentes penales: the certificate of no criminal record, demanded for formal work, which converts one prosecution into permanent exclusion.

details.aspect: The certificate is the gate to formal employment
details.description: Employers routinely require it, so a record excludes him from the formal sector and into ECO-001's informality permanently.
details.energy_note: One paper, and the formal economy closes.

details.aspect: Pretrial detention appears in the story regardless
details.description: Even without conviction, months of absence must be explained to an employer, and JUS-001 means many have them.
details.energy_note: Explaining a two-year gap that ended in acquittal.

details.aspect: The alternative employers are the ones from CAR-001
details.description: Exclusion from formal work leaves the offer described in CAR-001 as the best-paying option available, which is how the system recruits for itself.
details.energy_note: The only employer left is the one with the van.

details.aspect: SCENE - the certificate
details.description: The factory job needs the carta de no antecedentes penales. His shows the 2019 process. It also shows it was dismissed. The HR woman is sympathetic and says the system will not let her proceed with anything in the field at all, dismissed or not.
details.energy_note: Dismissed, and the box still cannot be ticked.

issues.title: The ball draw
issues.category_name: Conscription: the ball draw, and the year the state takes
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
issues.summary: Mexico conscripts by lottery, and only men are obliged to enter it. A year of Saturdays is allocated by drawing a coloured ball from a drum - one of the few hurdles in any of these datasets that applies to men and only men, explicitly, by law.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - obligatory for men, voluntary for women
details.description: Servicio Militar Nacional registration - alistamiento - is obligatory for all men on turning 18 and voluntary for women. Registration with SEDENA is required to obtain the Cartilla Militar.
details.energy_note: Compulsory if male, optional if not.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - what the colours mean
details.description: The draw is held on a Sunday in November. White ball: encuadramiento in the Army or Air Force with active training. Blue: assignment to the Navy. Black: exempt from active service - but not erased from military status; the man remains 'available' to the military command of his zone.
details.energy_note: Black is not freedom, it is availability.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - thirteen Saturdays
details.description: Those drawing white or blue complete thirteen consecutive Saturday sessions, 07:00 to 13:00. SEDENA says the format is designed not to interfere significantly with study or work.
details.energy_note: Three months of Saturdays.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - not turning up gets you the white ball
details.description: Historically, those who do not attend the draw automatically receive a white ball - so absence is not avoidance.
details.energy_note: Skip the lottery and you have already lost it.

details.aspect: The cartilla is an employment document
details.description: Completing the phases produces the released cartilla militar, valid for administrative and employment paperwork - so the man who avoids the whole thing lacks a document civilian employers ask for.
details.energy_note: A military paper he needs to get an office job.

details.aspect: It is the one hurdle here that is only about being male
details.description: Almost everything else in this file hits men disproportionately. The ball draw is the only item that names sex in the statute - which makes it the cleanest possible illustration of the `mexican_men` axis.
details.energy_note: The only one where the law itself says men.
details.notes: Design note: best single example of the applies_to intersection.

issues.title: Cobro de piso: paying to be allowed to trade
issues.category_name: Extortion, cobro de piso and the trades that get taxed
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Mexico, any gender
issues.summary: A weekly levy on small businesses, enforced by threat, which falls on the trades men predominantly run - shops, transport, farms, workshops.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - what it costs a business
details.description: ANPEC's president says the fee usually runs 500 to 1,000 pesos per week. ANPEC estimated in 2024 that cobro de piso takes between 10% and 20% of income for affected small businesses. Official figures quantifying it as a share of business income are otherwise lacking.
details.energy_note: A fifth of the takings, weekly, in cash.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the aggregate
details.description: Coparmex, the employers' association, put the cost to businesses at some $1.3 billion in 2023, and indicated losses of more than one billion dollars again in 2025.
details.energy_note: Over a billion dollars a year, in protection money.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - and almost none of it is reported
details.description: INEGI estimates 97% of extortion goes unreported. ENVIPE 2024 found extortion was the crime most reported by economic units of every size, with one in four victimised firms affected by it. Firm-level figures come from ENVE rather than ENVIPE.
details.energy_note: One business in four, and almost no complaints.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the trend and the new law
details.description: Extortion rose 10% nationally in Q1 2025; Mexico City cases nearly doubled in five months to 498 from 249. SESNSP recorded a record 5,887 extortion victims in H1 2025. A national strategy launched July 2025 and a federal law effective 29 November 2025 created a unified offence prosecutable without a complaint, with 15-25 year base sentences. SESNSP then reported a 38% decline; independent analysts question the methodology.
details.energy_note: A record, a new law, and a disputed improvement.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the polite young man on Friday
details.description: He is perhaps nineteen and he is not threatening. He says he knows the shop has been busy, asks after the daughter by name, and mentions that the price has gone up to 900 from next week. Then he buys a Coke and pays for it.
details.energy_note: He pays for the Coke. That is the part that frightens him.

details.aspect: The payment is what keeps him from reporting the payment
details.description: Once he has paid, he has participated, which he believes exposes him - so the first payment purchases the silence that protects all the subsequent ones.
details.energy_note: The first payment buys the silence for the rest.

issues.title: The trades that get taxed
issues.category_name: Extortion, cobro de piso and the trades that get taxed
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
issues.summary: Extortion is sector-specific: the businesses with visible daily cash, fixed premises or predictable routes, which are disproportionately run and staffed by men.

details.aspect: Tortillerías, combis, taxis, workshops
details.description: Fixed premises with daily cash and no capacity to relocate are the standard targets, along with transport on fixed routes.
details.energy_note: A route you cannot change is a route they can price.

details.aspect: Michoacán limes and avocados
details.description: Agricultural export crops with high value and a fixed growing location - limes and avocados - have been taxed at the orchard, a documented pattern in Michoacán.
details.energy_note: The tree cannot be moved, so the grower pays.

details.aspect: Closing the business is the common outcome
details.description: Where the levy exceeds the margin, the shop shuts - which removes the household income and hands the trade to whoever remains.
details.energy_note: He closes, after nineteen years.

details.aspect: Cargo and the long-haul driver
details.description: Highway cargo theft and driver extortion make long-distance trucking - an overwhelmingly male trade - a job with a violence premium built into it.
details.energy_note: Paid extra for the stretch after dark.

details.aspect: SCENE - closing the tortillería
details.description: Nineteen years. He sells the mill to a man from Celaya for less than it is worth and tells the regulars he is retiring. He is fifty-one. The shop reopens in five weeks under someone else, selling the same tortillas, and nobody asks him about it.
details.energy_note: Reopened in five weeks by somebody else.

issues.title: Bad hombres
issues.category_name: Being read as a criminal before you speak
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
issues.summary: A national political vocabulary that names Mexican men specifically as criminal, and the ordinary consequences of being the referent of a phrase everybody has heard.

details.aspect: The stereotype is about character, not competence
details.description: The content is criminality, dishonesty and threat rather than incapacity. As with the Nigerian case in the sibling dataset, a stereotype about honesty is worse than one about ability, because competence can be demonstrated and innocence cannot.
details.energy_note: He cannot prove the negative he is accused of.
details.notes: Structural parallel to PSY-001 in assets/text/nigeria.

details.aspect: It attaches to the men specifically
details.description: The rhetoric is gendered: the threatening figure invoked is male. Mexican women are stereotyped differently and not, in this particular vocabulary, as the danger.
details.energy_note: The word in the phrase is hombres.

details.aspect: It licenses behaviour from strangers
details.description: Being addressed in the street, followed in shops, or spoken to loudly and slowly are the everyday form, and each is individually too small to report - the mechanism catalogued as LNG in assets/text/abuse.
details.energy_note: Too small to report, forty times a year.
details.notes: See assets/text/abuse LNG-001 to LNG-010.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the parking lot
details.description: A man he has never met tells him to go back. He is forty-one, he has lived in this town for nineteen years, and he is holding a bag of groceries. He says nothing, because saying something is how this becomes an incident with his name in it.
details.energy_note: Silent, holding the shopping, doing the arithmetic.

issues.title: Priced into the dating market
issues.category_name: Being read as a criminal before you speak
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
issues.summary: The brief asked about men who are not dated because of what they are. There is measured platform data on this, and it is one of the better-evidenced rows in the psychological section.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the reply-rate gap
details.description: OkCupid's OkTrends data put average reply rates for male senders at Hispanic/Latino 25.2 against White 31.1, with Asian 25.3 and Black 22.6. Latino men sat near the middle-to-low end of the male sender hierarchy.
details.energy_note: Twenty-five per cent against thirty-one.
details.notes: 2009-2014 data, one platform. Recorded with that caveat.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - and it held across five years
details.description: Christian Rudder examined interactions between 2009 and 2014 involving more than 25 million people using QuickMatch ratings; the biases stayed fairly consistent across the period.
details.energy_note: Stable for five years running.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the asymmetry with Latina women
details.description: The same data put Hispanic/Latina women as senders at 46.8, close to White women at 47.4 and above Black women at 36.3; Rudder found Latina women among those rated best. The nationality is read very differently depending on the sex of the person carrying it.
details.energy_note: The same origin helps her and costs him.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - preemptive discrimination is the mechanism
details.description: Kevin Lewis, analysing over 126,000 OkCupid users, found people were more willing to reply across race lines than to initiate across them, and proposed that segregation occurs at the initiation stage because people anticipate rejection. The man does not message, because he expects not to hear back.
details.energy_note: He stops sending before anyone refuses him.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - and it is habit, not fixed preference
details.description: Lewis found that receiving a cross-racial message made people significantly more likely to cross racial boundaries themselves afterwards - an effect lasting about a week. Stated preferences are also comparatively open: only about 15% of Latino men and 16% of Latina women stated a same-race preference.
details.energy_note: It moves, and it moves back within a week.

details.aspect: The caveats matter and are recorded
details.description: The OkTrends figures are 2009-2014, single-platform, and predate swipe interfaces. Pew (July 2022) found 30% of US adults had used a dating site with no statistically significant differences by race/ethnicity, so outcome gaps are not explained by who joins. An Oxford study across 24 countries found in-group preference ranging from under 20% in Chile to over 80% in Slovakia, pointing to culture rather than biology.
details.energy_note: Old data, one platform, and culturally contingent.

issues.title: Being suspected at every counter
issues.category_name: Being read as a criminal before you speak
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Mexican nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: The cumulative administrative cost of being treated as a probable problem by banks, landlords, employers and officials.

details.aspect: Extra documentation, as standard
details.description: More proof of income, more deposit, a guarantor, a co-signer - each defensible individually and collectively a surcharge.
details.energy_note: Always one more document than the man in front.

details.aspect: Cash is suspicious and he is paid in cash
details.description: Informal and day-labour work pays cash (ECO-001, WRK-002), and cash deposits trigger scrutiny - so the employment condition produces the financial suspicion.
details.energy_note: Paid in the way that makes banks distrust him.

details.aspect: He pre-empts it, at his own cost
details.description: Carrying paperwork nobody asks of others, arriving early, dressing up for a routine appointment - unpaid, invisible, continuous.
details.energy_note: Dressed for court, to open a bank account.

details.aspect: SCENE - the deposit
details.description: The apartment asks first month, last month and a deposit - and then, for him, a co-signer with US credit history. He has been at the same job for six years and has the cash in an envelope. The cash is part of the problem.
details.energy_note: Having the money in cash counts against him.

issues.title: The deported man, at home
issues.category_name: Being read as a criminal before you speak
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
issues.summary: Return is not relief. Deportees are marked in Mexico - by accent, by tattoos, by the fact of having been sent back - and the stigma has a word.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - pocho
details.description: Richard Avila, deported at 56 after living in East Los Angeles since he was two, described Tijuana as feeling like being sent to the moon - not American, not Mexican, in bicultural limbo, where the way he spoke put a target on his back. Colleagues at the maquiladora called him pocho, a derogatory term for a Mexican who left.
details.energy_note: Foreign in the country of his own passport.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - 'how do you become Mexican'
details.description: One shelter worker described the disorientation directly: having grown up over there, not knowing the culture, feeling awkward about how he speaks and looks, because people can tell he is not from there. He has seen deportees without support become homeless, develop substance problems, or end up in prison.
details.energy_note: Asked to become a nationality he already legally is.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the criminal-record stigma travels with him
details.description: One call centre worker, Omar, asked that his surname not be used because of the stigma attached to deported convicts in Mexico, describing 21 years in prison and deportation three years earlier.
details.energy_note: Anonymous in his own country, about his own past.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - and the accent becomes the only asset
details.description: Tijuana's call centres grew from roughly 10 to more than 60 in two decades, most employing deportees, drawing work away from India on accent-neutral English at Mexican wages - 'Tijuana has become like the new Bombay,' per a recruiter of 16 years. Avila called it the best possible job for a deportee: better paid than construction or the maquiladora, and the first place his English was an asset rather than a scarlet letter.
details.money_note: Approx. monthly call centre pay, USD.
details.energy_note: The thing that marked him became the thing that paid him.

details.aspect: THE HONEST GAP - tattoos
details.description: The tattoo-as-gang-marker barrier is widely described anecdotally, and targeted searching did not surface sourced documentation of it as an employment barrier for deportees. Recorded as unverified rather than asserted.
details.energy_note: Everyone says it; nothing sourced found.

details.aspect: The word he uses for where he is from is now wrong in both places
details.description: Saying 'back home' in Tijuana means Los Angeles, and saying it in Los Angeles meant Michoacán. There is no sentence he can say about home that is not confusing to whoever is listening.
details.energy_note: No way to finish the sentence 'back home'.

issues.title: The pigmentocracy at home
issues.category_name: Discrimination inside Mexico: skin, class and language
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Mexico, any gender
issues.summary: Skin tone predicts schooling and earnings inside Mexico, measurably and substantially. Discrimination against Mexican men does not begin at the border.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the headline finding
details.description: Campos-Vázquez and Medina-Cortina, in Demography (2019), found people in the lightest skin colour category have on average 1.4 additional years of schooling and 53% higher hourly earnings than their darkest-skinned counterparts.
details.energy_note: Fifty-three per cent, for the shade of his skin.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - and it is a mobility effect, not just a level
details.description: Research on regional variance found that in every region analysed, the lightest-skinned group has a consistent advantage in upward social mobility. Villarreal (2010) found darker skin tones carry higher poverty risk and lower likelihood of affluence.
details.energy_note: Not just poorer - less able to stop being poor.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the gradient is steeper for men at the bottom
details.description: The colorist mobility pattern differs by sex: the gradient penalising darker skin is steeper for men starting at the bottom of the origin distribution, while the gradient in persistence at the top is steeper for women.
details.energy_note: Steepest for exactly this dataset's subject.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - measured several ways, including instruments
details.description: Evidence comes from PERLA (2010), INEGI's 2016 MMSI module, CEEY's 2017 EMOVI and ENADIS 2017. Solís, Güémez and Campos-Vázquez have benchmarked PRODER 2019 optical colorimeter readings against the PERLA palette, moving beyond interviewer classification. The PERLA project proposed the term pigmentocracy for the continent.
details.energy_note: Measured with an instrument, not an impression.

details.aspect: It is visible in advertising and casting
details.description: Who appears in Mexican television, advertising and politics is a daily public statement about which face belongs to which class, and a dark-skinned man sees it every day without it ever being said to him.
details.energy_note: Nobody says it. It is on every billboard.

details.aspect: The language of it is domestic and everyday
details.description: Güero, moreno, prieto, indio, naco, fresa - a dense everyday vocabulary for exactly the gradient DIS-001 measures, used affectionately, casually and as an insult, frequently by the same people in one conversation.
details.energy_note: A whole vocabulary for the thing nobody says exists.

issues.title: Indigenous, and that being a sentence
issues.category_name: Discrimination inside Mexico: skin, class and language
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Mexico, any gender
issues.summary: Indigenous Mexican men face compounded exclusion - language, documentation, land, and the internal agricultural migration circuit.

details.aspect: Justice in a language he does not speak
details.description: Interpreters for indigenous languages in criminal proceedings are a legal requirement and frequently unavailable, which interacts directly with POL-001's confession statistics.
details.energy_note: Confessing in Spanish to a document he cannot read.

details.aspect: The internal migration circuit
details.description: Triqui, Mixtec and Zapotec workers move to Sinaloa and Baja agricultural camps for the season, in conditions that are documented and poor - internal migration with many of the features of international migration.
details.energy_note: A migrant worker without leaving the country.

details.aspect: Late registration and DOC-001
details.description: Births registered late or not at all produce the documentation problems in DOC-001 at higher rates, so the exclusion is administrative before it is anything else.
details.energy_note: Excluded first by paperwork.

details.aspect: SCENE - the interpreter who does not come
details.description: The hearing proceeds in Spanish. He speaks Triqui. The public defender says he understands enough, and he nods, because nodding is what he has learned to do in rooms like this. He is asked whether he understands the charge and he says yes.
details.energy_note: Says yes, having understood roughly a third of it.

issues.title: The Chinese in Mexico: a massacre and an expulsion
issues.category_name: Discrimination inside Mexico: skin, class and language
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Mexico, any gender
issues.summary: The brief asked for weird, rare and non-obvious material. Mexico's own history of racial violence and mass expulsion is little known and well documented, and it complicates any simple account of who is excluded by whom.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - Torreón, May 1911
details.description: From 13 to 15 May 1911, 308 Chinese people were killed in Torreón, Coahuila - roughly half the city's Chinese community - by troops aligned with Francisco I. Madero during the Revolution. The first victims were agricultural workers killed in the orchards in the early hours of 13 May. Almost 100 Chinese businesses and homes were destroyed.
details.energy_note: Three hundred and eight people, in ten hours.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the finding, and the diplomatic aftermath
details.description: An investigation concluded the massacre was an unprovoked act of racial hatred, and a military tribunal appointed by Emilio Madero found the Maderista soldiers had committed atrocities. China demanded 30 million pesos in reparations. In 2021 President López Obrador apologised, saying the objective was to ensure it never happens again.
details.energy_note: Apologised for, one hundred and ten years later.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the Sonora and Sinaloa expulsions, 1931-33
details.description: Sonora and Sinaloa were the only states to carry out mass expulsions of Chinese men and their families - including families of Mexican origin. In 1931 the Sonoran government enacted discriminatory laws effectively banishing the Chinese; the mass expulsion ran 1931 to 1933. Several thousand were deported, some directly to China, others pushed through gaps in the international boundary fence into the United States, whose agents then deported the families onward to China.
details.energy_note: Pushed through a hole in the border fence by their own government.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - and Mexican women lost their nationality for marrying them
details.description: Mexican women were stripped of Mexican citizenship for marrying Chinese men. The expelled families arrived in Guangdong and eventually congregated in Macau.
details.energy_note: She married him and ceased to be Mexican.

details.aspect: Why it is in this dataset
details.description: It records that the state applying the hurdles in this file has itself expelled a minority by race within living memory of the grandparents of people now alive - which is context for DIS-001 and DIS-002 rather than a separate subject.
details.energy_note: The same state, doing the same thing, to someone else.
details.notes: Scholarly source: Julia María Schiavone Camacho, Chinese Mexicans (UNC Press, 2012); Julián Herbert on Torreón.

issues.title: Two surnames and a system with one box
issues.category_name: Names, surnames, screening and identity mismatch
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Mexican nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: Mexican naming convention meets foreign database design, and the result is a man who does not match himself across records.

details.aspect: Paternal and maternal surnames, truncated or swapped
details.description: Systems storing a single surname take one, drop one, or reverse them, so the boarding pass, the visa and the degree certificate disagree.
details.energy_note: Four documents, three versions of his name.

details.aspect: Accents and ñ do not survive
details.description: Diacritics are stripped or mangled between systems, producing mismatches that airline and immigration software treats as discrepancies.
details.energy_note: An accent that becomes a red flag.

details.aspect: It reads as an attempt to deceive
details.description: A name discrepancy is interpreted as possible deception rather than as a known limitation of the software, which is what turns a data problem into a secondary inspection.
details.energy_note: A software limitation, treated as a lie.
details.notes: Feeds AIR-001.

details.aspect: SCENE - four documents, three names
details.description: Boarding pass: RAMIREZDELGADO/JOSE. Visa: Jose Ramirez. Degree: José Ramírez Delgado. Bank: Jose R Delgado. The officer lays them side by side and asks which one is his actual name. All of them are.
details.energy_note: Asked to pick which of his names is the real one.

issues.title: Sharing a name with somebody
issues.category_name: Names, surnames, screening and identity mismatch
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Mexican nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: Common surnames plus watchlist matching produces men who are repeatedly stopped for someone else's record.

details.aspect: The match is on name and date of birth, not on him
details.description: Screening systems flag on limited identifiers, so a common surname with a common birth year produces recurring false positives.
details.energy_note: Stopped for a man he has never met.

details.aspect: Clearing it is not permanent
details.description: Redress processes exist, are slow, and frequently do not prevent the same flag recurring at the next port or the next airline.
details.energy_note: Cleared, and flagged again in March.

details.aspect: He cannot see the record that describes him
details.description: The underlying list entry is not disclosable, so he is managing a reputation he is not permitted to read.
details.energy_note: Correcting a file he is not allowed to see.

details.aspect: SCENE - the other José
details.description: The other man is six years older, was convicted in Texas in 2011, and shares his two surnames and his birth month. He has explained this at four airports. He now says it pre-emptively at the desk, which he has noticed makes it worse.
details.energy_note: Volunteering it early, which helps nothing.

issues.title: The officer who decided, and the one who would not have
issues.category_name: Discretion, clerical error and the officer who decided
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Mexican nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: Identical facts producing opposite outcomes depending on who is at the window - the defining experience of discretionary systems.

details.aspect: Same file, different answer
details.description: Visa applications, port-of-entry decisions and municipal permissions turn on a person rather than a rule, and the variance is invisible to the applicant.
details.energy_note: Refused Tuesday, approved Thursday, same papers.
details.notes: Same structure as GAT-007 in assets/text/abuse.

details.aspect: No reasons means nothing to correct
details.description: Where no written reasons are given, the applicant cannot fix the defect on reapplication, so the second attempt is a lottery too.
details.energy_note: Reapplying blind, at full price.

details.aspect: The queue is the punishment either way
details.description: Whichever way it goes, the wait was the same - so the cost is incurred before the discretion is exercised.
details.energy_note: He paid the year regardless of the answer.

details.aspect: SCENE - Thursday
details.description: Refused Tuesday, window 14. His neighbour - same town, same job, thinner file - approved Thursday, window 9. They compare the folders on the bus home and cannot find a single difference that would explain it, because there is not one.
details.energy_note: Two folders on a bus seat, no difference in them.

issues.title: The clerical error that becomes your record
issues.category_name: Discretion, clerical error and the officer who decided
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Mexican nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: A wrong keystroke in an official system, and the years spent proving the system is wrong about you.

details.aspect: Data propagates faster than corrections
details.description: An error copies between systems in seconds; the correction must be made in each one separately, by hand, in sequence.
details.energy_note: One mistake, eleven databases, one at a time.

details.aspect: The burden of proof is entirely his
details.description: The institution's record is presumed correct; he must produce documents disproving it, frequently from a third country.
details.energy_note: Presumed wrong about his own life.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the typo from 2011
details.description: A date of birth was entered wrong at a consulate in 2011. Every subsequent record inherited it. He is now told his passport does not match his visa history and he should resolve the discrepancy with the issuing authority - which is the body that made the error, and has no record of making it.
details.energy_note: Told to take it up with the people who did it.

issues.title: Four times more likely to kill himself
issues.category_name: Being male: help-seeking, machismo, and dying of it
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
issues.summary: Male suicide in Mexico runs at roughly four times the female rate, against a rising national trend - and the norms that produce it are the same ones that prevent him mentioning it.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the rates
details.description: As of 2016 Mexico's suicide rate was 5.2 per 100,000, up from 2.2 in 1990, with the male rate at 8.7 against 2.2 for women - close to four times. Male rates have consistently run around four times female rates.
details.energy_note: Four to one, and the total is rising.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - migration raises it on both sides of the line
details.description: Borges et al. (2009) found elevated risk of suicidal ideation among Mexicans with a family member in the United States, among Mexican-born immigrants who arrived aged 12 or younger, and among US-born Mexican Americans - with attempt risk also higher for those with family in the US.
details.energy_note: Having a brother in Texas raises his own risk, measurably.

details.aspect: The thing that would help is the thing he will not do
details.description: Help-seeking is the recognised protective behaviour and is precisely what the norm in MEN-002 suppresses.
details.energy_note: The treatment and the prohibition are the same subject.

issues.title: Machismo, measured
issues.category_name: Being male: help-seeking, machismo, and dying of it
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
issues.summary: The cultural expectation is not a cliché - it has been operationalised, measured, and associated with depression and reduced help-seeking, with effect sizes.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the meta-analytic association
details.description: Across eight quantitative studies (N = 3,413), a meta-analysis found a small-to-moderate positive association between traditional machismo and depressive symptoms (r = .243), with a similar correlation for broader emotional distress (r = .250).
details.energy_note: Measured, at r = .243.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - and it does not increase willingness to get help
details.description: A scoping review reports higher machismo endorsement linked to depression, stress, PTSD and suicidal ideation, and to lower rates of seeking mental health care - with evidence that machismo was linked to higher depressive symptoms but NOT to greater willingness to seek services, in both Mexican men and women.
details.energy_note: More symptoms, and no more likely to ask.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the literature distinguishes two things
details.description: Arciniega et al.'s (2008) Traditional Machismo and Caballerismo Scale separates traditional machismo from caballerismo - a prosocial, chivalrous dimension emphasising family and honour. Treating them as one construct is a known error.
details.energy_note: Two constructs, routinely collapsed into one slur.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - and the deficit story is too simple
details.description: A study of rural Mexican adults found largely positive help-seeking attitudes, often relying on familial support, with familismo connecting people to family and to services. Getrich et al. found machismo did not negatively affect colonoscopy screening. One study of Mexican American veterans found machismo related to both positive and negative mental health outcomes.
details.energy_note: It also holds families together, which is why it persists.

details.aspect: A methodological caveat worth keeping
details.description: Because machismo intersects with other social systems and spans multiple sub-domains, isolating its independent role in Latino mental health has proven difficult. The association is real and the causal share is not established.
details.energy_note: Real, and not cleanly separable from poverty.

issues.title: Not being read as a victim
issues.category_name: Being male: help-seeking, machismo, and dying of it
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by being male
issues.summary: The structural counterpart of VIO-001: men are the overwhelming majority of the killed and disappeared, and the least likely to be treated as victims by institutions, media or asylum systems.

details.aspect: The dead young man is presumed to have been involved
details.description: 'Andaba en algo' - he was into something - is the default public and frequently official reading of a murdered young man, which reduces investigative urgency and shames the family into silence.
details.energy_note: Assumed to have deserved it, by default.

details.aspect: Asylum frameworks are built around other profiles
details.description: Protection categories are more legible for women, families and children; a young man fleeing forced recruitment (CAR-001) presents as the demographic the system is screening for.
details.energy_note: Fleeing the gang makes him look like the gang.

details.aspect: He is less likely to be believed about fear
details.description: Credible-fear determinations turn on plausibility judgments in which a young man's account of being afraid is weighed against his appearance as a potential threat.
details.energy_note: Too big to be frightened, apparently.

details.aspect: THE HONEST GAP - the scholarship is thinner than the phenomenon
details.description: Femicide in Mexico is well theorised and well counted. Targeted searching did not surface a comparably developed body of work on why male victims of the same violence receive less investigative attention. This row records the gap rather than filling it with assertion.
details.energy_note: Widely observed, not well studied.

details.aspect: The game should let the player feel this one
details.description: The player as a Mexican man will be read as a threat by systems and as expendable by narrative - the same statistic used against him in both directions. That is the specific texture this difficulty setting should have, distinct from the Palestinian and Nigerian ones.
details.energy_note: Dangerous and disposable, from the same number.
details.notes: Design note: the tonal distinction between difficulty settings.

details.aspect: SCENE - the asylum interview
details.description: He explains that they came to his house and told him he would work for them. The officer asks why he did not go to the police, then asks whether he has tattoos, then asks him to describe the men again. He understands, watching the pen, that he is being assessed for membership rather than for fear.
details.energy_note: Describing being recruited, and being screened as a recruit.

issues.title: The provider who cannot provide
issues.category_name: Being male: help-seeking, machismo, and dying of it
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
issues.summary: Where a man's standing rests on supporting a household, unemployment, injury or deportation is not a financial event but an identity one.

details.aspect: The role is the whole standing
details.description: Where worth is measured by provision, losing the income removes the basis of his position in the family rather than reducing the budget.
details.energy_note: Not poorer. Diminished.

details.aspect: Which makes injury unreportable
details.description: Admitting he cannot lift it any more (OCC-002) threatens the role as well as the job, so pain is concealed from the family and the foreman alike.
details.energy_note: Hiding the back from his wife and his boss.

details.aspect: And makes the remittance non-negotiable
details.description: REM-002's requests cannot be declined without the refusal being read as a failure of the role, so he borrows rather than says no.
details.energy_note: Borrowing in order not to have to refuse.

details.aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the phone call he does not make
details.description: He lost the contract on Tuesday. It is Sunday and he has not told them. He calls at the usual hour, asks about his mother's knee, says work is fine, and sends money he has borrowed at 18%.
details.energy_note: Sends borrowed money rather than say the sentence.

issues.title: Informality means no health coverage
issues.category_name: The health system, and the illnesses that arrive early
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Mexico, any gender
issues.summary: Because more than half of Mexican work is informal, more than half of Mexican workers are outside the contributory health system - and the replacement schemes keep being restructured.

details.aspect: IMSS coverage follows the formal contract
details.description: Social security health coverage attaches to formal employment, so ECO-001's 55% informality rate is also a coverage statistic.
details.energy_note: Half the country, outside the system by definition.

details.aspect: The replacement has changed name and design repeatedly
details.description: Seguro Popular, then INSABI, then IMSS-Bienestar - each transition producing a period in which people were unsure what they were entitled to and where.
details.energy_note: Three schemes in a decade, and nobody knows which applies.

details.aspect: Out of pocket at the point of need
details.description: Catastrophic health spending falls on households directly, which is how a treatable illness becomes a debt or a sold plot of land.
details.energy_note: The operation costs the land.

details.aspect: SCENE - which one is it this year
details.description: His mother needs the medication monthly. Seguro Popular covered it. Then INSABI. Now it is IMSS-Bienestar and the pharmacy at the clinic says it is not arriving. He buys it privately for 1,400 pesos a month and stops asking which scheme he is in.
details.energy_note: Three national health schemes, one empty pharmacy shelf.

issues.title: Illnesses that arrive twenty years early
issues.category_name: The health system, and the illnesses that arrive early
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by anyone living in Mexico, any gender
issues.summary: Diabetes, kidney disease and cardiovascular illness at ages that would be unusual elsewhere, in a population doing heavy physical work.

details.aspect: Diabetes as a mass condition
details.description: Mexico carries one of the world's heaviest diabetes burdens, with complications - amputation, dialysis, blindness - arriving in working life rather than in old age.
details.energy_note: Dialysis at forty-six.

details.aspect: Dialysis is a full-time unpaid job
details.description: Three sessions a week ends most manual employment, converting a chronic illness into the loss of the household income described in MEN-004.
details.time_note: Approx. days per year in treatment.
details.energy_note: Three days a week, forever, and no job survives it.

details.aspect: Heat and kidneys
details.description: OCC-003's chronic kidney disease of non-traditional origin compounds this in agricultural populations on both sides of the border.
details.energy_note: The fields take the kidneys too.

details.aspect: SCENE - Monday, Wednesday, Friday
details.description: Dialysis at forty-six. Three mornings a week, four hours each, plus travel. No employer will take him on those terms and he has no contributions behind him because of the informality in ECO-001. His son leaves school at sixteen to drive a delivery route.
details.energy_note: His son leaves school so he can keep having dialysis.

issues.title: Treatment he will not seek
issues.category_name: The health system, and the illnesses that arrive early
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
issues.summary: Male under-use of preventive and primary care, compounded by language, cost and immigration fear where he is abroad.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - language multiplies the gap
details.description: Compared with older white men, older Mexican American men with high English proficiency are four times less likely to receive depression treatment, and those with low English proficiency ten times less likely. Latino men with low English proficiency had 2.5 times the likelihood of unmet mental health need compared with Latina women.
details.energy_note: Ten times less likely, for not speaking English.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - stigma predicts dropping out of care
details.description: Vega et al. (2010) found Latino men experiencing greater stigma were less likely to manage depressive symptoms or take medication, and missed more treatment appointments.
details.energy_note: The shame predicts the missed appointment.

details.aspect: Attending costs a shift he is paid by the hour for
details.description: Preventive care requires unpaid absence from hourly work, so the rational short-term choice is always to postpone.
details.energy_note: A check-up costs a day's pay and he is fine.

issues.title: The arithmetic that never stops
issues.category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
issues.summary: Continuous background computation - status, money, risk, who is behind him, what the officer will ask - running underneath every ordinary task.

details.aspect: It consumes the same capacity the work needs
details.description: Vigilance and contingency planning occupy working memory, so the cognitive cost shows up as ordinary tiredness and ordinary mistakes rather than as anything nameable.
details.energy_note: Not worried. Just slower, all the time.

details.aspect: Every routine act has a second calculation
details.description: Driving, being paid, going to a clinic, arguing with a landlord - each carries a second column nobody around him is computing.
details.energy_note: Two calculations where everyone else does one.

details.aspect: It is invisible and therefore uncredited
details.description: Colleagues see the output, not the overhead, so he is compared on equal terms with people running one process fewer.
details.energy_note: Judged against people carrying less.

details.aspect: SCENE - the indicator light
details.description: A bulb has gone on the rear plate. For anyone else it is a job for Saturday. For him it is a reason to be stopped, so he drives to the parts shop at ten at night, in the rain, and fixes it in the car park with a phone torch.
details.energy_note: Fixing a bulb at ten at night, because of what it could become.

issues.title: Not being able to plan
issues.category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
issues.applies_to_note: Triggered by Mexican nationality, passport or origin, anywhere
issues.summary: Where status, safety and income are all revocable at short notice, long-horizon planning stops being rational - which is then read as fecklessness.

details.aspect: The horizon shortens to match the uncertainty
details.description: Five-year plans are not made because the five years are not reliably his - see STA-002, JUS-001, DEP-001.
details.energy_note: No point planning a year he may not be in the country for.

details.aspect: Short horizons are then moralised
details.description: Not saving, not studying, not investing get attributed to character rather than to a correct assessment of volatility.
details.energy_note: Called short-sighted for seeing the situation accurately.

details.aspect: And it forecloses the goodlife triggers
details.description: Anything in the goodlife dataset requiring `documents`, `visa`, `credential` or a long time horizon is structurally unavailable, which is what the triggers column exists to model.
details.energy_note: Half the good things need a document he does not have.
details.notes: See assets/text/goodlife REQUIRE_TRIGGERS.

details.aspect: SCENE - the course he does not enrol on
details.description: Two years, evenings, and it would roughly double what he can charge. It also requires being in the same country for two years, which is not a thing he can promise. He closes the tab. He has closed this tab four times since 2021.
details.energy_note: The fourth time he has closed the same tab.

issues.title: Being the threat in the room
issues.category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
issues.summary: The daily management of other people's fear of him, and what continuous self-monitoring costs.

details.aspect: He softens himself continuously
details.description: Voice lowered, hands visible, distance kept, smile held - unpaid, constant impression management that nobody else in the lift is performing.
details.energy_note: Performing harmlessness, on a loop.

details.aspect: The cost is highest where the stakes are
details.description: In the traffic stop, the interview and the emergency room, the performance has to be perfect at exactly the moment he is most frightened.
details.energy_note: Must appear calmest when most afraid.

details.aspect: Anger is unavailable to him as a response
details.description: Legitimate anger confirms the stereotype and escalates the risk, so the ordinary human response to unfair treatment is closed off.
details.energy_note: Not allowed the reaction anyone else would have.

details.aspect: SCENE - the lift
details.description: A woman gets in on the fourth floor and he watches her decide something about him. He takes his hands out of his pockets, looks at his phone, and stands nearer the buttons than the wall. He is a quantity surveyor and he is forty-three.
details.energy_note: Rearranging himself in a lift, at forty-three.

issues.title: Enforcement fear as an ambient condition
issues.category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
issues.summary: The fear of a raid or a stop operates on whole communities including citizens, and changes behaviour far beyond the people actually removable.

details.aspect: It suppresses ordinary institutional contact
details.description: School engagement, clinic visits, benefit claims for citizen children and crime reporting all fall when enforcement is visible, including among people with status.
details.energy_note: Citizens stop going to the doctor too.

details.aspect: The children carry it
details.description: US-citizen children of removable parents show elevated anxiety and school difficulty tied to the possibility of return to an empty house.
details.energy_note: A nine-year-old rehearsing what to do if nobody is home.

details.aspect: It is a health exposure, not a mood
details.description: Community-level enforcement events have been studied as exposures with measurable downstream health effects rather than as sentiment.
details.energy_note: Studied like a pollutant, because that is how it behaves.

details.aspect: SCENE - the plan for if nobody comes
details.description: His daughter is nine. She knows the neighbour's door, the phone number written inside her pencil case, and not to open the door to anyone in a jacket. They practised it twice. She is a US citizen and has never been to Mexico.
details.energy_note: A nine-year-old citizen, rehearsing what to do if nobody comes home.

issues.title: What it takes out of the work
issues.category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
issues.summary: The brief asked specifically about efficiency and growth. This is the row that says what the load does to output and to a career.

details.aspect: Capacity spent on overhead is not spent on the job
details.description: PSY-001's continuous computation, PSY-003's impression management and OCC-002's pain all draw on the same finite daily budget as the work itself.
details.energy_note: Same budget, three more withdrawals.

details.aspect: Growth requires slack he does not have
details.description: Learning a new skill, taking a course, taking a risk on a better job - each needs spare capacity and a stable horizon, and PSY-002 removed the horizon.
details.energy_note: No spare capacity in which to become better paid.

details.aspect: The measured version exists in the construction data
details.description: OCC-002's Texas study found more pain sites produced more severe productivity loss, worst among those sleeping under six hours - so at least one link in this chain is quantified rather than asserted.
details.energy_note: One link of it is actually measured.

details.aspect: It compounds over a working life
details.description: Twenty years of slightly reduced capacity and foreclosed opportunity is not a bad year; it is a different career and a different pension.
details.energy_note: Not a bad year. A different life.

details.aspect: Compound interest, in reverse
details.description: Each foreclosed opportunity removes the platform for the next one, so the gap against an identical man without these hurdles widens every year rather than staying constant.
details.energy_note: The gap grows every year by itself.

details.aspect: SCENE - the foreman's job
details.description: They offer it to Danny, who has been there two years. He has been there nine. Nobody says anything about papers and nobody needs to - the role requires signing for deliveries, and signing requires being a person the company can put on a form.
details.energy_note: Nine years, and it goes to the man who can be put on a form.

issues.title: Divided across a line
issues.category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
issues.summary: Living in one country with the people he loves in another, permanently, and what that does over decades.

details.aspect: Missing the events that constitute a family
details.description: Funerals, births, graduations and illnesses happen without him, and the absences accumulate into not having been there for any of it.
details.energy_note: Absent from every photograph for eleven years.

details.aspect: He belongs fully to neither place
details.description: REP-004's pocho problem in Mexico and REP-001's hombre problem in the US leave no location where he is simply unremarkable.
details.energy_note: Foreign in both directions.

details.aspect: The return that keeps not happening
details.description: The plan to go back in two years is renewed annually for twenty, which is its own specific grief and is extremely common.
details.energy_note: Going home in two years, every year, for twenty.

details.aspect: SCENE - the funeral by phone
details.description: His father's funeral, held up to a camera by his sister so he can watch. The signal drops twice. Afterwards people tell him it was beautiful and that his father talked about him constantly, which is the part he cannot put down.
details.energy_note: Watched his father's funeral on a phone held up by his sister.

issues.title: Stress in the body, and the male-specific finding
issues.category_name: Somatic: what the load does to the body
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
issues.summary: The physiological cost of chronic stress is measurable as allostatic load - and in the largest Latino health study, the association held for men and not for women.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the finding, and its sex specificity
details.description: In HCHS/SOL, a sample of 3,848 Latinos across Cuban, Puerto Rican, Dominican, Mexican and South/Central American backgrounds found greater chronic and perceived stress significantly associated with allostatic load FOR MALES BUT NOT FEMALES, with ethnic background and nativity moderating the relationship for males.
details.energy_note: The stress-to-body pathway showed up in the men.
details.notes: The single most directly on-brief finding in this module: it is both about the body and specific to men.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - discrimination and cardiometabolic risk
details.description: An HCHS/SOL Sociocultural Ancillary Study analysis examined perceived discrimination against metabolic syndrome and its six components in 5,174 Hispanic/Latino adults, controlling for age, sex, income and acculturation. Related HCHS/SOL work found higher chronic stress burden associated with higher prevalence of coronary heart disease, hypertension and diabetes.
details.energy_note: It shows up as heart disease and diabetes.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - the Boston Puerto Rican Health Study
details.description: 882 Puerto Rican adults were assessed for major lifetime and everyday perceived discrimination against allostatic load across 11 physiological components. The authors note perceived discrimination is associated with type 2 diabetes, heart disease and hypertension, and with inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, oxidative stress and a steeper cortisol awakening response.
details.energy_note: Eleven physiological systems, measured.

details.aspect: THE HONEST GAP - the combined study does not exist
details.description: No single study was found combining perceived discrimination, cortisol and hypertension in Latino MEN within HCHS/SOL: the gendered allostatic load finding and the discrimination-cardiometabolic finding come from separate analyses. HCHS/SOL measures cortisol mainly via ancillary substudies. The chain is assembled from adjacent evidence and says so.
details.energy_note: Three findings that nobody has joined up.

details.aspect: Cortisol pathways are documented in Mexican-origin samples
details.description: Research in Mexican-origin adolescents and adults notes that discrimination experiences trigger cardiovascular activity and greater stress responses that over time contribute to allostatic load - so the mechanism is observed early in life.
details.energy_note: It starts in adolescence.

details.aspect: It is the same finding as the Nigeria dataset, in a different body
details.description: assets/text/nigeria SOM-002 found domestic-stress appraisal predicting low back pain at OR 2.88 in rural Nigerian women. This file finds chronic stress predicting allostatic load in Latino men and not women. Two populations, two designs, the same mechanism - which is why both datasets carry a SOM category.
details.energy_note: Same mechanism, opposite sexes, two continents.

issues.title: Depression arriving as a physical complaint
issues.category_name: Somatic: what the load does to the body
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
issues.summary: Where distress cannot be named, it presents to a doctor as pain, fatigue or stomach trouble - and is treated as those things.

details.aspect: The somatic idiom is the available one
details.description: MEN-002's norms make a back complaint sayable and a mood complaint not, so the back is what gets presented.
details.energy_note: He can say his back hurts. He cannot say the other thing.

details.aspect: Which produces the wrong treatment
details.description: Analgesia and physiotherapy for what is partly a mood disorder produces poor response, repeat attendance and a note about non-compliance - the mechanism in assets/text/abuse MED-002.
details.energy_note: Treated for the symptom he was able to mention.

details.aspect: The OCC-002 link runs both ways
details.description: Depressive symptoms were significantly associated with neck and shoulder pain in the North Carolina manual-worker study, so the distress and the pain are genuinely entangled rather than one masking the other.
details.energy_note: Both real, and feeding each other.

details.aspect: SCENE - what he tells the doctor
details.description: He says the back is bad and he is not sleeping. He does not say that he has been sitting in the truck for twenty minutes before going into the house each night, because he cannot think of the word for it and it is not what a back is. He is given ibuprofen and a leaflet on lifting.
details.energy_note: Given ibuprofen for the thing he could not name.

issues.title: Sleep
issues.category_name: Somatic: what the load does to the body
issues.applies_to_note: Requires both Mexican nationality and being male
issues.summary: Short sleep as the common pathway through which long hours, second jobs, pain and vigilance convert into everything else.

details.aspect: The hours simply are not there
details.description: ECO-002's working year plus commuting plus a second job leaves a sleep window measured in five or six hours.
details.energy_note: Five and a half hours, most nights, for years.

details.aspect: EXAMPLE - and it shows up directly in output
details.description: The Texas construction study found those sleeping under six hours were more severely affected by musculoskeletal pain in productivity terms.
details.energy_note: Under six hours, and the pain costs more.

details.aspect: Vigilance keeps him awake in the hours he has
details.description: PSY-001's background computation does not switch off at night, so the available window is not fully used either.
details.energy_note: In bed at eleven, asleep at two.
